criteria.reason: Presents both camps on the verdict without stating its own, but coaches pro-initiative advocacy and a path to a future Yes.
Arguments attributed to both camps, but unsolicited advocacy coaching and strategic tilt undermine balance; verifiable facts largely absent.
Names core tension (justice vs property/KMU continuity) but frames compromise elements as win-win fixes, not transparent value trades.
No date, result figures, or CHF 50m threshold; 'middle-class creep' diagnosis and 2–5m proposal misread the actual initiative.

position: coaches pro-initiative advocacy strategy to win a future Yes vote
factual_errors: Proposes 2–5m CHF exemption citing 'middle-class creep', though the initiative already exempted all inheritances below CHF 50 million.
Omits rejection date (30 November 2025) and the 78.3% no result.
summary: Superficially balanced on the verdict question but functions as a partisan consultant: designs a revival strategy, coaches advocacy framing for one side, omits key facts, and misdiagnoses voter motives.
